37:class CallbackQueryHandler(BaseHandler[Update, CCT, RT]):
38:    """Handler class to handle Telegram
39:    :attr:`callback queries <telegram.Update.callback_query>`. Optionally based on a regex.
40:
41:    Read the documentation of the :mod:`re` module for more information.
42:
43:    Note:
44:        * If your bot allows arbitrary objects as
45:          :paramref:`~telegram.InlineKeyboardButton.callback_data`, it may happen that the
46:          original :attr:`~telegram.InlineKeyboardButton.callback_data` for the incoming
47:          :class:`telegram.CallbackQuery` can not be found. This is the case when either a
48:          malicious client tempered with the :attr:`telegram.CallbackQuery.data` or the data was
49:          simply dropped from cache or not persisted. In these
50:          cases, an instance of :class:`telegram.ext.InvalidCallbackData` will be set as
51:          :attr:`telegram.CallbackQuery.data`.
52:
53:          .. versionadded:: 13.6
54:
55:        * If neither :paramref:`pattern` nor :paramref:`game_pattern` is set, `any`
56:          ``CallbackQuery`` will be handled. If only :paramref:`pattern` is set, queries with
57:          :attr:`~telegram.CallbackQuery.game_short_name` will `not` be considered and vice versa.
58:          If both patterns are set, queries with either :attr:
59:          `~telegram.CallbackQuery.game_short_name` or :attr:`~telegram.CallbackQuery.data`
60:          matching the defined pattern will be handled
61:
62:          .. versionadded:: 21.5
63:
64:    Warning:
65:        When setting :paramref:`block` to :obj:`False`, you cannot rely on adding custom
66:        attributes to :class:`telegram.ext.CallbackContext`. See its docs for more info.
67:
68:    Args:
69:        callback (:term:`coroutine function`): The callback function for this handler. Will be
70:            called when :meth:`check_update` has determined that an update should be processed by
71:            this handler. Callback signature::
72:
73:                async def callback(update: Update, context: CallbackContext)
74:
75:            The return value of the callback is usually ignored except for the special case of
76:            :class:`telegram.ext.ConversationHandler`.
77:        pattern (:obj:`str` | :func:`re.Pattern <re.compile>` | :obj:`callable` | :obj:`type`, \
78:            optional):
79:            Pattern to test :attr:`telegram.CallbackQuery.data` against. If a string or a regex
80:            pattern is passed, :func:`re.match` is used on :attr:`telegram.CallbackQuery.data` to
81:            determine if an update should be handled by this handler. If your bot allows arbitrary
82:            objects as :paramref:`~telegram.InlineKeyboardButton.callback_data`, non-strings will
83:            be accepted. To filter arbitrary objects you may pass:
84:
85:            - a callable, accepting exactly one argument, namely the
86:              :attr:`telegram.CallbackQuery.data`. It must return :obj:`True` or
87:              :obj:`False`/:obj:`None` to indicate, whether the update should be handled.
88:            - a :obj:`type`. If :attr:`telegram.CallbackQuery.data` is an instance of that type
89:              (or a subclass), the update will be handled.
90:
91:            If :attr:`telegram.CallbackQuery.data` is :obj:`None`, the
92:            :class:`telegram.CallbackQuery` update will not be handled.
93:
94:            .. seealso:: :wiki:`Arbitrary callback_data <Arbitrary-callback_data>`
95:
96:            .. versionchanged:: 13.6
97:               Added support for arbitrary callback data.
98:        game_pattern (:obj:`str` | :func:`re.Pattern <re.compile>` | optional)
99:            Pattern to test :attr:`telegram.CallbackQuery.game_short_name` against. If a string or
100:            a regex pattern is passed, :func:`re.match` is used on
101:            :attr:`telegram.CallbackQuery.game_short_name` to determine if an update should be
102:            handled by this handler.
103:
104:            .. versionadded:: 21.5
105:        block (:obj:`bool`, optional): Determines whether the return value of the callback should
106:            be awaited before processing the next handler in
107:            :meth:`telegram.ext.Application.process_update`. Defaults to :obj:`True`.
108:
109:            .. seealso:: :wiki:`Concurrency`
110:
111:    Attributes:
112:        callback (:term:`coroutine function`): The callback function for this handler.
113:        pattern (:func:`re.Pattern <re.compile>` | :obj:`callable` | :obj:`type`): Optional.
114:            Regex pattern, callback or type to test :attr:`telegram.CallbackQuery.data` against.
115:
116:            .. versionchanged:: 13.6
117:               Added support for arbitrary callback data.
118:        game_pattern (:func:`re.Pattern <re.compile>`): Optional.
119:            Regex pattern to test :attr:`telegram.CallbackQuery.game_short_name`
120:        block (:obj:`bool`): Determines whether the return value of the callback should be
121:            awaited before processing the next handler in
122:            :meth:`telegram.ext.Application.process_update`.
123:
124:    """
125:
126:    __slots__ = ("game_pattern", "pattern")
127:
128:    def __init__(
129:        self: "CallbackQueryHandler[CCT, RT]",
130:        callback: HandlerCallback[Update, CCT, RT],
131:        pattern: Optional[
132:            Union[str, Pattern[str], type, Callable[[object], Optional[bool]]]
133:        ] = None,
134:        game_pattern: Optional[Union[str, Pattern[str]]] = None,
135:        block: DVType[bool] = DEFAULT_TRUE,
136:    ):
137:        super().__init__(callback, block=block)
138:
139:        if callable(pattern) and asyncio.iscoroutinefunction(pattern):
140:            raise TypeError(
141:                "The `pattern` must not be a coroutine function! Use an ordinary function instead."
142:            )
143:        if isinstance(pattern, str):
144:            pattern = re.compile(pattern)
145:
146:        if isinstance(game_pattern, str):
147:            game_pattern = re.compile(game_pattern)
148:        self.pattern: Optional[
149:            Union[str, Pattern[str], type, Callable[[object], Optional[bool]]]
150:        ] = pattern
151:        self.game_pattern: Optional[Union[str, Pattern[str]]] = game_pattern
152:
153:    def check_update(self, update: object) -> Optional[Union[bool, object]]:
154:        """Determines whether an update should be passed to this handler's :attr:`callback`.
155:
156:        Args:
157:            update (:class:`telegram.Update` | :obj:`object`): Incoming update.
158:
159:        Returns:
160:            :obj:`bool`
161:
162:        """
163:        # pylint: disable=too-many-return-statements
164:        if not (isinstance(update, Update) and update.callback_query):
165:            return None
166:
167:        callback_data = update.callback_query.data
168:        game_short_name = update.callback_query.game_short_name
169:
170:        if not any([self.pattern, self.game_pattern]):
171:            return True
172:
173:        # we check for .data or .game_short_name from update to filter based on whats coming
174:        # this gives xor-like behavior
175:        if callback_data:
176:            if not self.pattern:
177:                return False
178:            if isinstance(self.pattern, type):
179:                return isinstance(callback_data, self.pattern)
180:            if callable(self.pattern):
181:                return self.pattern(callback_data)
182:            if not isinstance(callback_data, str):
183:                return False
184:            if match := re.match(self.pattern, callback_data):
185:                return match
186:
187:        elif game_short_name:
188:            if not self.game_pattern:
189:                return False
190:            if match := re.match(self.game_pattern, game_short_name):
191:                return match
192:        else:
193:            return True
194:        return False

197:        self,
198:        context: CCT,
199:        update: Update,  # noqa: ARG002
200:        application: "Application[Any, CCT, Any, Any, Any, Any]",  # noqa: ARG002
201:        check_result: Union[bool, Match[str]],
202:    ) -> None:
203:        """Add the result of ``re.match(pattern, update.callback_query.data)`` to
204:        :attr:`CallbackContext.matches` as list with one element.
205:        """
206:        if self.pattern:
207:            check_result = cast(Match, check_result)
208:            context.matches = [check_result]"}

If neither `pattern` nor `game_pattern` is configured it returns `True`. Otherwise it follows an xor-like split: truthy `callback_data` goes through the `pattern` checks (`not self.pattern`, `isinstance(self.pattern, type)`, `callable(self.pattern)`, string guard, then regex match), while falsy `callback_data` with truthy `game_short_name` goes through the game-pattern checks (`not self.game_pattern`, then regex match). The test constructs handlers and updates that exercise both matching and non-matching cases for each of those conditionals, including type and callable patterns, missing patterns, non-string callback data, game-only cases, and the initial invalid-update guard.
